title: NSS runbook: Cloud NSS new, stopped, missing and delayed logs, parsing errors and the SIEM connectivity test errors

new-instance-subscriptions.statement: For a newly deployed or migrated Cloud NSS, the runbook checks the subscriptions in the Admin Console, notes an instance can be provisioned but not fully enabled on the backend, and says to follow the working-setup scope if it is enabled but shows unhealthy.

quotes: Check if the Cloud NSS subscriptions are reflecting appropriately on Zscaler Admin Console under Administration > Account Management > Subscriptions.
Sometimes the instance might be provisioned but not fully configured and enabled on the backend. Make sure you have a confirmation from the Zscaler Account team regarding the provisioning.
If the instance is enabled and ready for use, but shows unhealthy, then follow the next scope (working setup) for further troubleshooting.

recently-stopped.statement: For a setup that recently stopped working, the runbook runs the Admin Console SIEM connectivity test; if the console shows healthy but the SIEM gets no logs it continues with Logs are Missing.

quotes: Run the Zscaler Admin Console connectivity test towards the SIEM.
If the Zscaler Admin Console shows healthy, but no logs are received on the SIEM, then proceed with Logs are Missing.
Setup that Recently Stopped Working

missing-logs-prechecks.statement: Cloud NSS missing-logs prechecks: instance and SIEM in the same Geo, Cloud NSS IP ranges allowlisted by region, at least one active feed, private Nanolog reachable, Max Batch Size sized per the deployment guide, and any SIEM rate calculated from log volume and EPS.

quotes: Make sure the provisioned Cloud NSS instance and your SIEM are in the same Geo.
You should allow list the Cloud NSS server IP address ranges on required ACLs, depending on the region.
You must have configured at least one feed and make it active.
If you are using private Nanolog cluster, make sure Cloud NSS can reach the private Nanolog.
Proper sizing of Max Batch Size is done and configured on the Cloud NSS during deployment, as per the respective deployment guide.
If a SIEM rate (rate limiting) is configured in the feed, make sure that this has been well calculated using the log volume and EPS limitation on the user side.

error-routing-reachability.statement: For Cloud NSS connectivity-test errors, reachability errors (SIEM Host not Reachable, SIEM Host Port not Reachable) mean confirming the SIEM listens on the configured IP and port, and generic errors (SIEM Host down, SIEM Host unresponsive) mean validating the SIEM topology and allowlisting the Cloud NSS IPs if needed.

quotes: For errors related to reachability, such as SIEM Host not Reachable or SIEM Host Port not Reachable, make sure SIEM is listening on the configured IP and port.
For generic connectivity errors such as SIEM Host down or SIEM Host unresponsive, etc., understand the SIEM network topology and validate it. If necessary, add allow list for Zscaler Cloud NSS IPs.

error-routing-response.statement: Errors about the SIEM response (Error in SIEM authentication, Invalid SIEM redirect response) go to the SIEM team, SSL certs missing for SIEM Host means contacting Zscaler to add certs, Invalid SIEM URL format means validating the feed's SIEM configuration, and Zscaler internal errors mean a support ticket.

quotes: For errors related to SIEM response such as Error in SIEM authentication or Invalid SIEM redirect response, etc., involve the SIEM team to take necessary action.
If you see the error SSL certs missing for SIEM Host, contact Zscaler to add required certs.
If you see the error Invalid SIEM URL format, validate the SIEM configuration in the Cloud NSS feed.
Zscaler internal errors: Raise a ticket with Zscaler Support for further investigation.

logs-delayed-batch-size.statement: In its Logs are Delayed steps the runbook checks Max Batch Size against its 16 KB default and recommends 512 KB for Splunk, Sumologic and other SIEM types, 8 MB for S3, and 1 MB for DNS, Tunnel and other log types such as SaaS Security.

quotes: Check if the Max Batch Size is configured to the default of 16 KB. Increase the value to 512 KB for Splunk, Sumologic, and other SIEM types.
For S3, the recommended maximum batch size is 8 MB.
For DNS, Tunnel, and all other log types (e.g., SaaS Security), the recommended size is 1 MB.
Logs are Delayed

logs-delayed-siem-rate.statement: In its Logs are Delayed steps the runbook says to perform all the prechecks described in the previous section, checks that SIEM Rate is an optimal value for the log volume and SIEM EPS, and has Zscaler Support take packet captures.

quotes: Perform all the prechecks described in previous section.
Check if you have the SIEM Rate configured in the feed, and make sure it is an optimal value depending on the log volume and SIEM EPS.
Contact Zscaler Support for taking packet captures and investigating any network or connectivity issues.
Logs are Delayed

parsing-400.statement: A connectivity test returning a 400 response code is the indicator of SIEM parsing errors.

quotes: The indicators of SIEM parsing issues are that a connectivity test returns a 400 response code when there are parsing errors on SIEM side.

parsing-checks.statement: For SIEM parsing issues the runbook checks SIEM event logs, that correlation rules are enabled, the Feed Escape Character, that the feed format uses hex-encoded fields for string fields like url and useragent, and says JSON Array Notation can be enabled for troubleshooting if it was disabled.

quotes: Check for errors/warnings in the SIEM event logs.
Confirm that any relevant correlation rules are enabled for the Cloud NSS feed.
Make sure the appropriate Feed Escape Character is configured in the Feed config.
Make sure you are using hex-encoded fields in the feed format for the string fields like url, useragent, etc.
If you have disabled JSON Array Notation, you can enable this for troubleshooting purposes when there are parsing errors.

json-array-notation.statement: JSON Array Notation lets the NSS stream a batch of logs as a JSON array: individual logs ordered in a list, separated by commas and surrounded by square brackets.

quotes: This setting allows the NSS to stream a batch of logs in a JSON Array format.
Individual logs are ordered in a list, separated by commas, and surrounded by square brackets
If you have disabled JSON Array Notation, you can enable this for troubleshooting purposes when there are parsing errors.

json-escape-character.statement: For a JSON-format feed the runbook says the escape character should always be ,/" and describes it as comma, backslash, double quote.

quotes: If JSON format is chosen, the escape character should always be ,/" (comma, backslash, double quote).

siem-test-flow.statement: The Admin Console SIEM connectivity test request flows from CA to the NSS to the Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB) to the SIEM, with ZAB doing a sample log upload and passing back the response.

quotes: This UI-initiated test request flows through CA, to the NSS, to the Zscaler Authentication Bridge, to the SIEM, with the response returning along the same path.
Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB) performs a sample upload of logs to the SIEM and passes back the response.

siem-test-response.statement: A successful SIEM connectivity test returns a 200-series response code, and any other code is the actual error code returned by the SIEM, indicating an issue between ZAB and the SIEM.

quotes: A successful test returns a response code in 200 series.
Any response code other than 2XX indicates an issue in the connectivity between ZAB and SIEM. This is the actual error code returned by SIEM.

siem-test-exceptions-network.statement: Some SIEM test errors are exceptions, not SIEM responses: NoRouteToHostException is SIEM Host not Reachable, PortUnreachableException is SIEM Host Port not Reachable, UnknownHostException is Invalid SIEM Hostname, NoHttpResponseException is SIEM Host busy, ConnectTimeout and HttpHostConnectException are SIEM Host down, SocketTimeoutException is SIEM Host unresponsive.

quotes: Sometimes there could be exceptions encountered that are not the actual response from SIEM, such as timeout exceptions while trying to connect to SIEM.
| NoRouteToHostException | SIEM Host not Reachable |
| PortUnreachableException | SIEM Host Port not Reachable |
| UnknownHostException | Invalid SIEM Hostname - Failed to resolve the Hostname |
| NoHttpResponseException | SIEM Host busy |
| ConnectTimeout | Exception SIEM Host down |
| HttpHostConnectException | SIEM Host down |
| SocketTimeoutException | SIEM Host unresponsive |

siem-test-exceptions-protocol.statement: In the SIEM test, SSLHandshakeException shows SSL certs missing for SIEM Host, SSLException shows SSL Error, ProtocolException HTTP shows Error with SIEM Host, MalformedChallengeException shows Error in SIEM authentication, RedirectException shows Invalid SIEM redirect response, URIException shows Invalid SIEM URL format, RuntimeException shows Error parsing SIEM URL.

quotes: | SSLHandshakeException | SSL certs missing for SIEM Host |
| SSLException | SSL Error |
| ProtocolException HTTP | Error with SIEM Host |
| MalformedChallengeException | Error in SIEM authentication |
| RedirectException | Invalid SIEM redirect response |
| URIException | Invalid SIEM URL format |
| RuntimeException | Error parsing SIEM URL |

siem-test-exceptions-internal.statement: In the SIEM test, UnknownException shows Zscaler Internal Error 0, BindException 1, ConnectionPoolTimeoutException 2, SocketExceptions 3 and IOExceptions 4.

quotes: | UnknownException | Zscaler Internal Error 0 |
| BindException | Zscaler Internal Error 1 |
| ConnectionPoolTimeoutException | Zscaler Internal Error 2 |
| SocketExceptions | Zscaler Internal Error 3 |
| IOExceptions | Zscaler Internal Error 4 |

json-escape-notation.summary: The runbook writes the JSON feed escape character as ,/" with a slash, while the general NSS feed guidelines write it as ,\" with a backslash.

quotes: If JSON format is chosen, the escape character should always be ,/" (comma, backslash, double quote).

positions.says: The escape character is written ,/" and described as comma, backslash, double quote.

quotes: To prevent the issue, enter a comma, backslash, and quotation marks (,\") as the Feed Escape Character and use hex-encoded fields (e.g., %s{elogin}instead of %s{login}) in the Feed Output Format.

positions.says: Enter a comma, backslash and quotation marks, written ,\", as the Feed Escape Character.

json-escape-notation.impact: The runbook's ,/" has a slash where its own description and the feed guidelines have a backslash. Do not give an admin ,/" to type; give the feed guidelines' form and say the runbook writes it differently.

non-2xx-meaning.summary: The runbook's parsing steps say a 400 response from the connectivity test indicates SIEM parsing errors, while its SIEM test description says any non-2XX response indicates a connectivity issue between ZAB and the SIEM.

quotes: The indicators of SIEM parsing issues are that a connectivity test returns a 400 response code when there are parsing errors on SIEM side.

positions.says: A 400 from the connectivity test indicates SIEM parsing errors.

quotes: Any response code other than 2XX indicates an issue in the connectivity between ZAB and SIEM. This is the actual error code returned by SIEM.

positions.says: Any non-2XX response code indicates a connectivity issue between ZAB and the SIEM.

non-2xx-meaning.impact: A 400 is both a parsing indicator and a non-2XX connectivity-issue response. Do not tell an admin a 400 is only parsing, or only connectivity; check the SIEM side.
